newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Japan says info-tech deal ball in EU court.
newsitem.headline: Japan says info-tech deal ball in EU court.

text.p: Ministers from the United States, Japan, Canada and the European Union on Tuesday told their working level officials to pull together an agreement to scrap tariffs on information technology products quickly and be flexible in doing so, a Japanese foreign ministry official said.

"Concerning the issues of non-tariff measures and the timetable (for eliminating tariffs), we are getting over the hump. If the EU is not hardline on these, we can pull them together," the official said on Tuesday.
But the issue of which products to include in the sought-after pact to scrap tariffs by the year 2000 remained tough and would require political decisions, he added.

The United States, strongly backed by Japan, has been pushing for an agreement to eliminate tariffs in the lucrative and fast-growing world info-tech market at the first ministerial meeting of the World Trade Organisation here.
The EU also wants a deal, but has been arguing that it needs to include steps to prevent non-tariff barriers from offsetting the benefit of tariff removal.
Each of the four countries, meanwhile, has "sensitive" products it wants to leave out of the deal.

The Big Four trade powers are trying to get agreement amongst themselves while calling on other WTO members, especially the Asian-Pacific nations that are key exporters of such technology, to join in. And they want to achieve their aim of an ITA by the time the WTO conference ends on Friday.
"We may be running a bit late, but the negotiations are getting more focused," the official said.
